version_note: Verb + Noun format with plain-English explanations. Validated.

leaves.examples_raw: Put whatever the agent is currently using — recent inputs, intermediate results — onto a "scratch pad" for quick access.
Save past events as "episodes" — which game was won, which plan failed, what happened step by step — like a personal diary.
Save general facts about the world — "fire is hot", "404 means not found" — not tied to any specific event.

leaves.action: Process perceptual inputs into textual observations
leaves.examples_raw: Turn images, sounds, or sensor readings into text descriptions so a text-based LLM can understand the physical world.

leaves.action: Affect physical environments via robotic planners
leaves.examples_raw: Actually move things in the real world — pick up a cup, open a door — by sending language commands to a robot arm.

leaves.action: Convert images to text via VLMs
leaves.examples_raw: Feed a picture to a Vision-Language Model (like GPT-4V) and get back a text description of what's in it.
Receive a task or command from a human user, e.g. "book me a flight" or "translate this paragraph."
When something is unclear, proactively ask the human — "Which file did you mean?"
Chat casually, tell jokes, do role-play — provide emotional support or fun.
Have multiple agents argue different sides of the same question, using the debate to reach a better answer.
Split a big job among multiple agents — one writes code, one tests, one documents — and combine the results.

leaves.action: Interact with games, APIs, and websites
leaves.examples_raw: Operate in digital environments: play Minecraft, call a weather API, click buttons on a webpage.
Run a piece of code and get the output — e.g. run a Python script, execute a database query.
Call outside tools to fill knowledge gaps or handle heavy math — look up a database, use a calculator, etc.

leaves.action: Load skills from the skill library
leaves.examples_raw: Find and load a ready-made code snippet from a pre-built library — e.g., grab the "chop tree" skill in Minecraft.
Search the "diary" for relevant past experiences, ranked by how recent, important, and relevant they are.
Look up reference docs (API docs, tutorials) and use that information to help write code.
Pull a general fact from the knowledge base — e.g., look up "what does HTTP 404 mean?"
Check the "scratch pad" — grab the intermediate results and state information stored there.
Condense a flood of recent information into a few key takeaways to avoid information overload.

Extract the core conclusion from a pile of raw data — "so the real issue is X."
For every binary score z(q) i,j from the judge, there is a corresponding explanation e(q)i,j. (P3)

leaves.action: Provide context for subsequent LLM calls
leaves.examples_raw: Package the reasoning results so far and feed them as background into the next LLM call for a better answer.
Save a full action sequence from start to finish — every step recorded — for later training or review.
Change the model's internal weights through training so it actually performs better on similar tasks — real learning.
Instead of changing weights, build a case library of past experiences and look up the closest match when a new problem arrives.
Generalize from raw experiences into reusable facts and save them — e.g., after three failures, note "this API has a rate limit."
Do a post-mortem on what went wrong, store the lessons learned, and avoid making the same mistake again.
Use a Vision-Language Model to scan the environment and produce a labeled map — not just layout, but annotations like "door here" or "enemy there."
Adjust the large language model's weights using supervised learning, reinforcement learning, or human feedback to improve on a specific task.
Have the LLM produce multiple outputs, pick the best ones, and train on those — the model bootstraps its own improvement.
Use smaller, specialized models for specific jobs — one for summarization, one for SQL — instead of one big model for everything.

leaves.action: Update the source code as procedural memory
leaves.examples_raw: Modify the agent's own source code — essentially patching itself to change how it behaves.
Look at a few "input → output" examples, figure out the underlying rule, and use that rule as a prompt for future tasks.
Rewrite its own prompt template so the LLM thinks more clearly next time — learning a better way to reason.
Write or improve code snippets that interact with the outside world — e.g., learn a new way to navigate a webpage.
Keep a syllabus of mastered and upcoming skills, arranged by difficulty, so the agent learns in a sensible order.
Improve how the agent searches for information — e.g., better keyword strategies or smarter relevance ranking.
Improve the decision process itself — e.g., go from "pick randomly" to "score every option and pick the best."
Brainstorm "what could I do right now?" — generate one or more possible next moves.

leaves.action: Evaluate actions via heuristics, LLM, or learned values
leaves.examples_raw: Score each candidate: use rules of thumb, ask the LLM to judge, or use a trained value function to estimate how good each option is.
Mentally rehearse an action before doing it — imagine "if I do X, what will the environment look like?" without actually executing.

leaves.action: Select actions via argmax, softmax, or majority vote
leaves.examples_raw: Pick one action to execute: take the highest-scored one (argmax), sample probabilistically (softmax), or let multiple evaluators vote.

leaves.action: Execute grounding actions, API calls, or learning actions
leaves.examples_raw: Finally, do it for real: either perform an external action (call an API, move a robot) or an internal one (update memory, fine-tune).
